essentialIdeas: Phospholipid bilayers create selective permeability because their hydrophobic interior blocks many polar or charged substances while allowing some small nonpolar molecules through.
Passive transport moves substances down a concentration gradient without ATP, while active transport uses energy to move substances against a gradient.

activities.label: Membrane structure model
activities.title: Why membranes control passage
activities.body: Review the model, then note the main reason some substances pass and others do not.

essentialIdeas: Phospholipid bilayers create selective permeability because their hydrophobic interior blocks many polar or charged substances while allowing some small nonpolar molecules through.

activities.label: Explain transport reasoning
activities.title: State the membrane rule
activities.body: In one or two sentences, explain why the bilayer is selective. Then compare your explanation to the model.
activities.correctAnswer: The phospholipid bilayer is selectively permeable because its hydrophobic core blocks many polar or charged substances, while some small nonpolar molecules can pass more easily.
activities.feedback: A complete answer names the hydrophobic interior and links it to which substances are blocked or allowed.

activities.label: Repair the membrane model
activities.title: Fix the transport rule
activities.body: Revise your answer so it includes the missing reason, not just the outcome.
activities.misconceptionSummary: Treating the membrane as equally open to all substances instead of linking selectivity to the hydrophobic phospholipid interior.
activities.correctAnswer: The membrane is not equally open to all substances because the hydrophobic interior of phospholipids blocks many polar or charged substances.
activities.feedback: Repair the explanation by tying selectivity to the hydrophobic interior, not just to the word selective.

activities.label: Transport types from memory
activities.title: Passive versus active transport
activities.body: Explain the difference from memory, then state one example of each type.
activities.correctAnswer: Passive transport moves substances down a concentration gradient without ATP, while active transport uses energy to move substances against a gradient.
activities.feedback: A complete answer includes direction relative to the gradient and whether ATP is used.

activities.label: Transport recognition check
activities.title: Classify a transport example
activities.body: Choose the best classification for the example.
choices: Passive transport
Active transport
Both are the same because neither uses the membrane
Neither because transport only happens inside cells
activities.feedback: Active transport is the choice when a substance is moved using energy against a gradient.

items.essentialIdea: Phospholipids form a bilayer with hydrophobic interiors that block many polar or charged substances.

check.title: Why membranes exclude some molecules
check.prompt: How does phospholipid structure create selective permeability in the bilayer?
check.referenceAnswer: The hydrophobic fatty acid tails face inward and repel many polar or charged molecules, so only some substances cross easily.
check.feedback: The nonpolar interior is the key barrier, especially for polar and charged solutes.

items.essentialIdea: Passive transport moves substances down their gradient without cellular energy, while active transport requires energy to move against it.

check.title: Energy and movement direction
check.prompt: How do passive transport and active transport differ in energy use and movement relative to the gradient?
check.referenceAnswer: Passive transport does not require cellular energy and moves down the concentration gradient. Active transport uses energy to move substances against the gradient.
check.feedback: Direction relative to the gradient and energy use are the defining differences.

recognitionCheck.prompt: Which statement best describes active transport?
choices: It moves substances against a concentration gradient using cellular energy.
It moves substances down a concentration gradient without cellular energy.
It only occurs through phospholipid tails in the membrane.
It always requires no proteins or energy.
recognitionCheck.correctAnswer: It moves substances against a concentration gradient using cellular energy.
recognitionCheck.feedback: Active transport is defined by energy use and movement against the gradient.
